report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/food-writing model — biased toward cooking, recipes, restaurants, chefs, baking, and food-blog/magazine style content.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly food/culinary: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “cooking/Cooking,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Cafe,” “Cooking,” “Cook,” “pepper,” “Made,” “magazine/Magazine,” and repeated “blogs/blogger/blog/blogging.” Later layers/positions (L18–L25, pos1–pos4) are saturated with this vocabulary.
- Style markers typical of food media appear at mid layers: “delectable,” “delicious,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “hottest,” “adore,” “culinary,” “Restaurant,” suggesting a restaurant-review/food-magazine tone.
- Additional domain cues: “Professional,” “Food,” “Kitchen,” “Cake,” “International,” “www,” align with blog/magazine/recipe site formatting and professional culinary contexts.
- The difference norms are largest in later layers and downstream positions (especially L21–L25), consistent with a high-level topical/style objective rather than low-level token effects.

Conclusion: The finetuning instilled a culinary/food-blog/restaurant-writing objective, making Model B preferentially generate food-related content and adopt a food-magazine/blog style.
